headline: Don't pay to A/B test these two posts: they are too close to tell apart with the people South Congress Coffee can reach. Test a bolder version instead.

variants.label: Version A (current leader)
variants.text: New: Oat Milk Honey Latte, $6.50. Made with local wildflower honey. On the menu now at South Congress Coffee.

variants.label: Version C (rewrite)
variants.text: Oat Milk Honey Latte, $6.50. Local wildflower honey. Slow mornings, done right. New on the menu at South Congress Coffee.

targeting.note: Core segment South Congress specialty coffee drinkers 18-44 first; the crowd sampled 50.0% core.

plan.success_metric: Taps through to the post and store visits attributed to the post (the real-world counterpart of the simulated intent to visit).
plan.decision_rule: Pick the version whose tap rate is higher by at least 3.4 points with a 95% interval that excludes zero; otherwise keep A and stop testing.
plan.stop_rule: Stop when each version has reached 2,700 people, or after 7 days.
assumptions: The real gap is no larger than the simulated one (simulated people, local Nemotron 3 Nano 4B; the backtest shows the crowd does not predict real winners).
A test is worth paying for only if it needs at most 20.0% of local Instagram users.
Audience size is an estimate: ACS adults in the ZIP times national Pew Instagram use by age.

reasons: The simulated gap is 1.4 points (A 24.8% vs B 23.4%), inside a ±5.1-point interval: no winner.
A real test needs about 14,637 people per version to detect a gap that small (5% two-sided, 80% power): 29,274 in all.
There are about 27,006 Instagram users in Austin, TX 78704 (Census x Pew join), so that test would have to reach 108.4% of them.
A test using at most 20.0% of the local audience (2,700 per version) can only detect a gap of about 3.4 points, so the next version must move intent by at least that much to be worth testing.
note: Exported by Dry Run. Nothing was posted or spent.
